title: Hybrid tripeptides incorporating 5-aminoisophthalate: structural insights into supramolecular assembly, dye adsorption and Cu 2+  sensing
content: Incorporation of 5-aminoisophthalate (AIA) as a rigid aromatic γ-amino acid into short hybrid peptides provides an effective strategy for directing supramolecular organisation. Herein, two tripeptides, Boc-Xx-Aib-AIA (OMe)2 (Xx = l-Leu (1) and l-Trp (2)), were synthesized, and both peptides adopted distorted β-turn conformations stabilised by intramolecular ten- and five-membered hydrogen-bonding interactions. Peptide 1 formed a zig–zag chain leading to a pleated supramolecular sheet-like architecture, whereas peptide 2 assembled into a rippled sheet, influenced by the indole side chain. SEM analysis revealed an entangled fibrillar network with interstitial voids in the peptide assemblies. These fibrillar networks exhibited efficient adsorption of cationic dyes from aqueous solutions, demonstrating their potential as recyclable adsorbents. Additionally, peptide 2 showed a distinct response to Cu2+ ions, as evidenced by UV-vis spectroscopy. These findings establish AIA-incorporated hybrid tripeptides as tuneable building blocks that afford distinct supramolecular organisation and functional properties, providing a useful platform for the design of peptide-based materials with tailored properties.
